headline: Plans for a City of Lights Parade float and a Veterans Recognition Program nomination.
summary: Other items cover a UMass Lowell hockey night, a Golden Gloves vendor table, and a new meeting place. Updates to member listings, the website, and business cards also appear.
items: Guest speaker Emily Forbes postponed; she has applied and may speak in February
Future meeting place needed while the Lowell Telemedia Center is under construction after a water leak
Follow-up on the Trunk or Treat event sponsored by the Vet Center of Lowell
Follow-up on the Veterans Day event
UMass Lowell hockey night during Veterans Day appreciation night
Vendor table requested at the Golden Gloves Veterans Appreciation Night
City of Lights Parade float on Saturday, 11/28/26, honoring Veterans, with decorating at 11:00 AM
Veterans Recognition Program nomination; William "Bill" McDevitt recommended
Honoring a Lowell High School ROTC student and Lowell Police cadet for a lifesaving rescue
Possible speakers: State Representative Tara Hong and the new UMass Lowell Student Veteran Alliance president
How Veterans can join the commission, and updates to the city website
Google email account, website, and social media still being set up

Securing Lowell Memorial Auditorium for the 11/10/27 Veterans Day event

location: DPD Conference Room, above Police Station, 50 Arcand Drive, Lowell, MA
plain_text:
AGENDA 
LOWELL VETERANS COMMISSION MEETING 
DATE: Wednesday, 18th November 2026 at 5:00 PM 
DPD Conference Room, above Police Station, 50 Arcand Drive, Lowell, MA 
Enter using the door that says DPD 
 
Meeting: 
a. Call to Order: 
b. Pledge of Allegiance  
c. Roll Call Attendance  
 PARADISE, PAUL 
 GAFFNEY, JAMES III 
 COTE, RICHARD A. 
PEEPLES, MICHAEL 
 CEROVAC, ROBERT  
 GAUTHIER, PHILIAS  
 PEEPLES, JEAN, SUB COMMITTEE MEMBER 
 ERIC LAMARCHE, DIRECTOR OF VETERANS’ SERVICES 
 
1. Guest Speaker Emily Forbes of the Veterans Administration has been postponed.  Veterans Commission 
member Jay Gaffney reports a new policy for speakers addressing outside groups has been implemented by 
the Veterans Administration. Emily has applied and is optimistic about a February meeting. 
 
2. The meeting place of future Veterans Commission meetings is needed as the Lowell Telemedia Center is 
still under construction following a water leak. Alternate locations for the 12/09/26 meeting are the Mayor’s 
Reception Room, the Council Chambers, the Senior Center or the Library.  Veterans Commission member 
Jay Gaffney has been taking care of setting up meetings.   
 
3. Follow up for the Trunk or Treat Event sponsored by the Vet Center of Lowell, which the Veterans 
Commission participated in.  The display was a depiction from the movie “Animal House” and candy was 
given out to all guests.  Veterans Commission members were dressed up as characters from the movie. 
 
4. Follow up for Veterans Day Event.  Special thanks to all who participated. 
 
5. UMass Lowell Hockey night (during the Veterans Day appreciation night).  There was no response to our 
letter to President Meehan.  Secretary Peeples met with Ted Seroczynsky, Director of Military and Veterans 
Services of UMass Lowell and they will follow up in coordinating the Students and Faculty of UML in 
participating in Veterans Commission events and honoring Veterans. 
 
6. Participation by the Veterans Commission at the Golden Gloves Veterans Appreciation Night (usually held 
in February).  The Veterans Commission would like to host a vendor table at this event. 
 
7. City of Lights Parade:
a. The Veterans Commission will participate in providing a float in the City of Lights Parade to honor 
Veterans.  Chairman Paul Paradise offered his truck and flatbed to provide the transportation.  The 
Commission members will participate in decorating the float.  An idea to have a holiday tree 
decorated in red, white, and blue lights, an eagle at the top of the tree, American Flags, bunting, US 
Military logos, and banners saying sponsored by the Veterans Commission of Lowell.  The date is 
Saturday, 11/28/26.  The parade starts on Jackson Street and staging will be from 1:00 PM to 4:00 
PM with the Parade starting at 4:30 PM. 
   
Eric will provide the banner: Sponsored by the Veterans Commission. 
Waiver is needed for all participants. 
Theme is Lowell at 200 (for the City’s Bicentennial year). 
Flags, bunting, military logos, banners 
Silhouette of Soldier that says, “All Gave Some, Some Gave All.” 
Suggestion for Banners on both side of the float… Thank You Lowell Veterans, who made Lowell’s 
200 Bicentennial possible. 
Suggestion to meet at the home of Secretary Michael Peeples to decorate the float on Saturday 
11/28/26 at 11:00 AM (prior to the staging that starts at 1:00 PM). 
 
8. The Veterans Recognition Program  
 
A nomination for the Veterans Recognition Program has been made by Ted Serozynsky, Director Military 
and veterans Services of UMass Lowell. 
 
Not sure if he’s ever been recognized before, but reading your description for Veterans Appreciation, I 
might recommend William “Bill” McDevitt out of our office here. Born and raised in Lowell (I believe), 
Vietnam combat vet / US Army, retired from the U.S. Post Office before starting a 2nd career at UMass 
Lowell, and has been helping our student vets for the last 14(ish) years. Not sure if that counts for the 
city (school is within the city, etc). Recently works with our disabled student vets receiving benefits 
under Chapter 31 Veteran Readiness and Employment. Also a member of both the DAV and Lowell 
VFW. 
 
I’m sure there’ll be others that come to mind as time goes on, but Bill was too obvious to overlook (he 
and Nancy, our PT staff, often reminisce about growing up in Lowell – they were in the same Lowell HS 
class!) 
 
9. New Business: 
 
a. Paul Paradise provided details of a Lowell High School ROTC Student and Lowell Police Cadet’s 
lifesaving heroics in saving an autistic child from drowning.  Plans are needed to honor the student at 
a future meeting. 
b. Meet and greet to speak at the Veterans Commission meetings.  Suggestion: State Representatives 
Tara Hong. 
c. Ted Serozynsky, Director of Military and Veterans Services of UMass Lowell introduced the new 
incoming Student Veteran Alliance President of UMass Lowell to Secretary Michael Peeples during
a Veterans Event at UML.  This individual would also make a great speaker during the Veterans 
Commission meeting. 
d. Ted Serozynsky, Director Military and Veterans Services of UMass Lowell asked for updated 
information on how Veterans can join the Veterans Commission.  He would like to post the 
information at UMass Lowell.  The City of Lowell’s website may need updating. 
e.  Google email is soon to release the Veterans Commission GMail account, and the files will be 
available to access.  The Veterans Commission Website and social media platforms (Facebook page) 
are still under construction. 
f. Order new business cards for the Veterans Commission. 
g. Secure the Lowell Memorial Auditorium for next year’s Veterans Day Event 11/10/27.  Wreaths 
Across America confirmed application for their participation and it is free. 
h. Clerical updates to the listing of Veterans Commission members listed on the City of Lowell’s 
Website is needed.  Williams, Hayley, city of Lowell Health Department has been working with 
Secretary Michael Peeples to update minutes and agendas and may be helpful in updating more.  The 
current listing of Veteran Commission members are (the Veterans Commission is comprised of up to 
11 members): 
• Chair: Paul Paradise 
• Member: Jacquelynn Coles 
• Member: Richard A. Cote  
• Member: Walter O’Neil, Jr. 
• Member: James Harmon 
• Member: James J. Gaffney, III 
• Member: Kenneth Wedge  
• Member: Vacant 
  Needed updating Member Secretary Michael Peeples 
  Needed updating Member Vice Chair Robert Cerovac 
  Needed updating Member Philias Gauthier 
   Needed update of Meetings: The Veterans Commission meets on the 2nd Wednesday 
   of each month at 5:00 PM. 
   Needed update of how Veterans can join the Veterans Commission. 
 
10. Approval of meeting Minutes of Veterans Commission meeting of 10/14/26.  
_______________________________________________________________________ 
Regularly scheduled meetings of the Lowell Veterans Commission are held on the 2nd Wednesday of the 
month Lowell Telemedia Center, 246 Market St, Lowell, MA 01852 starting at 5:00 PM. The following is 
a list of scheduled meetings: September 9, 2026, October 14, 2026, November 11, 2026 (rescheduled to
November 18, 2026), December 9, 2026, January 13, 2027, February 10, 2027, March 10, 2027, April 14, 
2027, May 12, 2027, and. June 9, 2027.
